sentences.en: "I felt a Funeral, in my Brain, and Mourners to and fro kept treading -- treading -- till [it seemed] that Sense was breaking through -- And when they all were seated,
sentences.zh: "我在我的脑海中感觉到一个丧葬, 和摩尔人不停地走动, 一直走动,直到思念破碎。 当他们都坐着的时候,

sentences.en: a Service, like a Drum -- kept beating -- beating -- till I [thought] my Mind was going numb -- And then I heard them lift a Box and creak across my Soul
sentences.zh: 服务,就像鼓声, 不停地打, 不停地打, 直到我脑筋麻木—— 然后我听到他们举起一个盒子, 在我的灵魂上翻滚。

sentences.en: with those same Boots of Lead, again, then Space -- began to toll, As [all] the Heavens were a Bell, and Being, [but] an Ear, and I, and Silence, some strange Race,
sentences.zh: 以同样的铅靴,然后是太空--开始造成伤亡,因为诸天是钟声,是耳声,我和沉默,是奇异的赛跑,

sentences.en: wrecked, solitary, here -- [And] then a Plank in Reason, broke, and I fell down and down -- and hit a World, at every plunge,
sentences.zh: 残废的,孤独的,在这里--然后是理性的木板,破碎的,我跌倒的-- 在每个跳梯上,都撞到一个世界。

sentences.en: and Finished knowing -- then --" We know depression through metaphors.
sentences.zh: (笑声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声) (掌声(掌声) (掌声)

sentences.en: Emily Dickinson was able to convey it in language, Goya in an image.
sentences.zh: Emily Dickinson能够用语言传达,用图像传达Goya。

sentences.en: Half the purpose of art is to describe such iconic states.
sentences.zh: 艺术的一半目的是描述这些标志性状态。

sentences.en: As for me, I had always thought myself tough, one of the people who could survive if I'd been sent to a concentration camp.
sentences.zh: 至于我 我总是觉得自己很坚强 如果我被送到集中营 就能活下来的人之一

sentences.en: In 1991, I had a series of losses. My mother died, a relationship I'd been in ended, I moved back to the United States from some years abroad, and I got through all of those experiences intact.
sentences.zh: 1991年,我遭受了一系列损失。我母亲去世了,我结束了一段关系, 我从国外几年回到了美国, 我度过了所有这些经历。

sentences.en: But in 1994, three years later, I found myself losing interest in almost everything.
sentences.zh: 但是在1994年,三年后, 我发现自己对几乎所有事情都失去了兴趣。

sentences.en: I didn't want to do any of the things I had previously wanted to do, and I didn't know why.
sentences.zh: 我不想做我以前想做的事 我不知道为什么

sentences.en: The opposite of depression is not happiness, but vitality.
sentences.zh: 抑郁的反面不是幸福 而是活力

sentences.en: And it was vitality that seemed to seep away from me in that moment.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻,生命力似乎离我而去。

sentences.en: Everything there was to do seemed like too much work.
sentences.zh: 在那里所做的一切 似乎太多的工作。

sentences.en: I would come home and I would see the red light flashing on my answering machine, and instead of being thrilled to hear from my friends, I would think, "What a lot of people that is to have to call back."
sentences.zh: 我会回家,我会看到红灯 闪烁在我的答录机上, 而不是激动 听到我的朋友, 我想,"什么是很多人 需要打电话回来。"

sentences.en: Or I would decide I should have lunch, and then I would think, but I'd have to get the food out and put it on a plate and cut it up and chew it and swallow it, and it felt to me like the Stations of the Cross.
sentences.zh: 或者我会决定我应该吃午饭,然后我会想, 但我必须把食物拿出来 放在盘子上,切开它,嚼断它,吞掉它, 它感觉就像十字架。

sentences.en: And one of the things that often gets lost in discussions of depression is that you know it's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 在关于抑郁症的讨论中 常常会失去的一件事 就是你知道这很荒谬

sentences.en: You know it's ridiculous while you're experiencing it.
sentences.zh: 你知道这是荒谬的 当你正在经历它。

sentences.en: You know that most people manage to listen to their messages and eat lunch and organize themselves to take a shower and go out the front door and that it's not a big deal, and yet you are nonetheless in its grip
sentences.zh: 你知道,大多数人 设法听 他们的信息,吃午餐 并组织自己 淋浴和走出前门

sentences.en: and you are unable to figure out any way around it.
sentences.zh: 你无法找到任何办法

sentences.en: And so I began to feel myself doing less and thinking less and feeling less.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始觉得自己做得少 思考少 感觉少

sentences.en: It was a kind of nullity. And then the anxiety set in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种无效,然后是焦虑。

sentences.en: If you told me that I'd have to be depressed for the next month, I would say, "As long I know it'll be over in November, I can do it."
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉我 下个月我不得不沮丧, 我会说, "我早就知道它会在11月结束,我可以做到这一点。"

sentences.en: But if you said to me, "You have to have acute anxiety for the next month," I would rather slit my wrist than go through it.
sentences.zh: 但是如果你对我说,“你下个月必须感到极度焦虑,” 我宁愿割断我的手腕,也不愿通过它。

sentences.en: It was the feeling all the time like that feeling you have if you're walking and you slip or trip and the ground is rushing up at you, but instead of lasting half a second, the way that does, it lasted for six months.
sentences.zh: 这是那种感觉 你一直有这种感觉 如果你走,你滑倒,或旅行, 地面正在冲上你, 但是没有持续半秒, 这样做的方式, 它持续了六个月。

sentences.en: It's a sensation of being afraid all the time but not even knowing what it is that you're afraid of.
sentences.zh: 这是一种一直害怕但又不知道自己害怕什么的感觉。

sentences.en: And it was at that point that I began to think that it was just too painful to be alive, and that the only reason not to kill oneself was so as not to hurt other people.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我开始觉得活着实在是太痛苦了，不自杀的唯一原因就是为了不伤害别人。

sentences.en: And finally one day, I woke up and I thought perhaps I'd had a stroke, because I lay in bed completely frozen, looking at the telephone, thinking, "Something is wrong and I should call for help,"
sentences.zh: 最后有一天，我醒来，我想我可能中风了，因为我躺在床上完全冻僵了，看着电话，心想：“出了什么问题，我应该打电话寻求帮助，”

sentences.en: and I couldn't reach out my arm and pick up the phone and dial.
sentences.zh: 我无法伸出手臂拿起电话拨打。

sentences.en: And finally, after four full hours of my lying and staring at it, the phone rang, and somehow I managed to pick it up, and it was my father, and I said, "I'm in serious trouble. We need to do something."
sentences.zh: 最后，在我躺着盯着它看了整整四个小时之后，电话铃响了，不知怎的，我设法接了起来，是我父亲打来的，我说，“我遇到了严重的麻烦。我们需要做点什么。”

sentences.en: The next day I started with the medications and the therapy.
sentences.zh: 第二天我开始接受药物和治疗。

sentences.en: And I also started reckoning with this terrible question: If I'm not the tough person who could have made it through a concentration camp, then who am I?
sentences.zh: 我也开始思考这个可怕的问题：如果我不是一个能够挺过集中营的坚强的人，那么我是谁？

sentences.en: And if I have to take medication, is that medication making me more fully myself, or is it making me someone else?
sentences.zh: 如果我必须服药，这种药物是让我更加完整地做自己，还是让我成为另一个人？

sentences.en: And how do I feel about it if it's making me someone else?
sentences.zh: 如果它让我变成了另外一个人，我会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I had two advantages as I went into the fight.
sentences.zh: 当我参加战斗时，我有两个优势。

sentences.en: The first is that I knew that, objectively speaking, I had a nice life, and that if I could only get well, there was something at the other end that was worth living for.
sentences.zh: 首先，我知道，客观地说，我过着美好的生活，如果我能康复，那么另一端就有值得为之而活的东西。

sentences.en: And the other was that I had access to good treatment.
sentences.zh: 另一个是我可以获得良好的治疗。

sentences.en: But I nonetheless emerged and relapsed, and emerged and relapsed, and emerged and relapsed, and finally understood I would have to be on medication and in therapy forever.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然出现并复发，出现并复发，出现并复发，最后明白我必须永远接受药物治疗和治疗。

sentences.en: And I thought, "But is it a chemical problem or a psychological problem?
sentences.zh: 我想，“但这到底是化学问题还是心理问题？

sentences.en: And does it need a chemical cure or a philosophical cure?"
sentences.zh: 它需要化学疗法还是哲学疗法？”

sentences.en: And I couldn't figure out which it was. And then I understood that actually, we aren't advanced enough in either area for it to explain things fully.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那是什么。然后我明白了，实际上，我们在这两个领域都还不够先进，无法充分解释事情。

sentences.en: The chemical cure and the psychological cure both have a role to play, and I also figured out that depression was something that was braided so deep into us that there was no separating it from our character and personality.
sentences.zh: 化学疗法和心理疗法都可以发挥作用，而且我还发现抑郁症是一种深深扎根于我们内心的东西，以至于它与我们的性格和个性密不可分。

sentences.en: I want to say that the treatments we have for depression are appalling.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我们对抑郁症的治疗方法令人震惊。

sentences.en: They're not very effective. They're extremely costly.
sentences.zh: 它们不是很有效。它们非常昂贵。

sentences.en: They come with innumerable side effects.
sentences.zh: 它们有无数的副作用。

sentences.en: They're a disaster. But I am so grateful that I live now and not 50 years ago, when there would have been almost nothing to be done.
sentences.zh: 他们是一场灾难。但我很庆幸自己生活在现在，而不是 50 年前，那时几乎无事可做。

sentences.en: I hope that 50 years hence, people will hear about my treatments and be appalled that anyone endured such primitive science.
sentences.zh: 我希望 50 年后，人们会听到我的治疗方法，并对有人忍受如此原始的科学感到震惊。

sentences.en: Depression is the flaw in love. If you were married to someone and thought, "Well, if my wife dies, I'll find another one," it wouldn't be love as we know it.
sentences.zh: 抑郁是爱情中的缺陷。如果你嫁给某人并想：“好吧，如果我的妻子去世了，我会再找一个”，那么这就不是我们所知道的爱。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as love without the anticipation of loss, and that specter of despair can be the engine of intimacy.
sentences.zh: 没有对失去的预期就没有爱情，而绝望的幽灵可能是亲密的引擎。

sentences.en: There are three things people tend to confuse: depression, grief and sadness.
sentences.zh: 人们容易混淆三件事：抑郁、悲伤和悲伤。

sentences.en: Grief is explicitly reactive. If you have a loss and you feel incredibly unhappy, and then, six months later, you are still deeply sad, but you're functioning a little better, it's probably grief,
sentences.zh: 悲伤显然是被动反应的。如果你有一个损失,你感到令人难以置信的不快乐, 然后,六个月后,你仍然非常伤心, 但你的功能好一点了, 它可能是悲伤,

sentences.en: and it will probably ultimately resolve itself in some measure.
sentences.zh: 它可能最终会 解决自己在某种程度上。

sentences.en: If you experience a catastrophic loss, and you feel terrible, and six months later you can barely function at all, then it's probably a depression that was triggered by the catastrophic circumstances.
sentences.zh: 如果你经历了一场灾难性的损失,你感到可怕, 6个月后,你几乎无法发挥任何功能, 那么它很可能是一个抑郁症, 是由灾难性的情况引发的。

sentences.en: The trajectory tells us a great deal. People think of depression as being just sadness.
sentences.zh: 轨迹告诉我们很多。人们认为抑郁只是悲伤。

sentences.en: It's much, much too much sadness, much too much grief at far too slight a cause.
sentences.zh: 太多太多的悲伤 太多的悲伤 太多的悲伤 过轻一个原因。

sentences.en: As I set out to understand depression, and to interview people who had experienced it, I found that there were people who seemed, on the surface, to have what sounded like relatively mild depression
sentences.zh: 当我开始理解抑郁症, 并采访曾经经历过抑郁症的人时, 我发现有些人,表面上似乎 听起来像相对温和的抑郁症

sentences.en: who were nonetheless utterly disabled by it.
sentences.zh: 然而,他们却因它而完全残废。

sentences.en: And there were other people who had what sounded as they described it like terribly severe depression who nonetheless had good lives in the interstices between their depressive episodes.
sentences.zh: 还有其他人,他们把声音描述成 极度严重的抑郁症, 但他们在他们忧郁的中间 有着良好的生活。

sentences.en: And I set out to find out what it is that causes some people to be more resilient than other people.
sentences.zh: 我开始寻找是什么 导致一些人比其他人更有弹性。

sentences.en: What are the mechanisms that allow people to survive?
sentences.zh: 允许人们生存的机制是什么?

sentences.en: And I went out and I interviewed person after person who was suffering with depression.
sentences.zh: 我出去采访了 患有抑郁症的人

sentences.en: One of the first people I interviewed described depression as a slower way of being dead, and that was a good thing for me to hear early on because it reminded me that slow way of being dead
sentences.zh: 我采访的第一批人之一 将抑郁描述为一种较慢的方式 死亡, 这是一件好事,我听到 早期,因为它提醒我 缓慢的方式 死亡

sentences.en: can lead to actual deadness, that this is a serious business.
sentences.zh: 可能导致实际死亡, 这是一项严肃的工作。

sentences.en: It's the leading disability worldwide, and people die of it every day.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上主要的残疾, 每天都有人死于它。

sentences.en: One of the people I talked to when I was trying to understand this was a beloved friend who I had known for many years, and who had a psychotic episode in her freshman year of college,
sentences.zh: 我试图了解的其中一个人 是一个我认识多年的深爱的朋友 她大学大一时精神失常

sentences.en: and then plummeted into a horrific depression.
sentences.zh: 然后跌到可怕的萧条中

sentences.en: She had bipolar illness, or manic depression, as it was then known.
sentences.zh: 她患有双极性疾病,或狂躁抑郁症,正如当时所知。

sentences.en: And then she did very well for many years on lithium, and then eventually, she was taken off her lithium to see how she would do without it, and she had another psychosis, and then plunged into the worst depression that I had ever seen
sentences.zh: 之后她对锂做了很多年的很好, 最终,她脱下锂 去看没有锂她会怎么做, 然后她又有了另一个精神错乱症, 然后跳进了我所见过的最糟糕的抑郁症中。

sentences.en: in which she sat in her parents' apartment, more or less catatonic, essentially without moving, day after day after day.
sentences.zh: 在她父母的公寓里, 或多或少是精神紧张症, 基本上不动, 日复一日地。

sentences.en: And when I interviewed her about that experience some years later -- she's a poet and psychotherapist named Maggie Robbins -- when I interviewed her, she said, "I was singing 'Where Have All The Flowers Gone,'
sentences.zh: 几年后,当我采访她时, 她是一个诗人和精神病治疗师 名叫玛姬·罗宾斯—— 当我采访她时,她说,“我唱着“花都到哪儿去了,”

sentences.en: over and over, to occupy my mind. I was singing to blot out the things my mind was saying, which were, 'You are nothing. You are nobody.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍,我不停地想着,我唱着 抹去我心里所说的话,当时说,“你什么都不是,你什么都不是。

sentences.en: You don't even deserve to live.' And that was when I really started thinking about killing myself."
sentences.zh: 那时我开始想自杀"

sentences.en: You don't think in depression that you've put on a gray veil and are seeing the world through the haze of a bad mood.
sentences.zh: 你没有在忧郁中 想到你戴了灰色面纱 并且看到世界通过 坏心情的烟雾。

sentences.en: You think that the veil has been taken away, the veil of happiness, and that now you're seeing truly.
sentences.zh: 你以为面纱被拿走了 幸福的面纱 现在你真的看到了

sentences.en: It's easier to help schizophrenics who perceive that there's something foreign inside of them that needs to be exorcised, but it's difficult with depressives, because we believe we are seeing the truth.
sentences.zh: 帮助精神分裂症患者比较容易 因为他们认为他们体内有些异质 需要驱魔 但抑郁症很难 因为我们相信我们看到了真相

sentences.en: But the truth lies. I became obsessed with that sentence: "But the truth lies."
sentences.zh: 但真相是谎言,我沉迷于这句话:"但真相是谎言"

sentences.en: And I discovered, as I talked to depressive people, that they have many delusional perceptions.
sentences.zh: 我发现,当我和忧郁的人交谈时, 他们有许多妄想感。

sentences.en: People will say, "No one loves me." And you say, "I love you, your wife loves you, your mother loves you."
sentences.zh: 人们会说,“没有人爱我。” 然后你说,“我爱你,你的妻子爱你,你的母亲爱你。”

sentences.en: You can answer that one pretty readily, at least for most people.
sentences.zh: 至少对大多数人来说 你可以轻易回答这个问题

sentences.en: But people who are depressed will also say, "No matter what we do, we're all just going to die in the end."
sentences.zh: 但忧郁的人也会说,“不管我们做什么,我们终究都会死。”

sentences.en: Or they'll say, "There can be no true communion between two human beings.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会说,“两个人之间不可能有真正的圣餐。

sentences.en: Each of us is trapped in his own body." To which you have to say, "That's true, but I think we should focus right now on what to have for breakfast."
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都被困在自己的身体里。” 你不得不说,“这是真的,但我想我们现在应该 专注于早餐吃什么。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) A lot of the time, what they are expressing is not illness, but insight, and one comes to think what's really extraordinary is that most of us know about those existential questions
sentences.zh: (笑) 很多时候, 他们表达的不是疾病, 而是洞察力, 并且人们开始思考 什么是真正的非同寻常

sentences.en: and they don't distract us very much. There was a study I particularly liked in which a group of depressed and a group of non-depressed people were asked to play a video game for an hour, and at the end of the hour,
sentences.zh: 他们不会让我们分心。有一个研究 我特别喜欢,在研究中 一群忧郁症和一群非忧郁的人 被要求玩一个小时的游戏, 到了最后,

sentences.en: they were asked how many little monsters they thought they had killed.
sentences.zh: 他们被问及他们杀了多少个小怪物

sentences.en: The depressive group was usually accurate to within about 10 percent, and the non-depressed people guessed between 15 and 20 times as many little monsters -- (Laughter) as they had actually killed.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症群体通常精确到大约10%, 而非抑郁症患者的猜测是他们实际杀死的 15到20倍的小怪物--(笑声)

sentences.en: A lot of people said, when I chose to write about my depression, that it must be very difficult to be out of that closet, to have people know.
sentences.zh: 很多人说,当我选择 写我的抑郁症, 一定是非常困难 出柜,让人们知道。

sentences.en: They said, "Do people talk to you differently?"
sentences.zh: 他们说,“人们和你说话不一样吗?”

sentences.en: I said, "Yes, people talk to me differently.
sentences.zh: 我说,"是的,人们跟我说话不同。

sentences.en: They talk to me differently insofar as they start telling me about their experience, or their sister's experience, or their friend's experience.
sentences.zh: 他们对我说话的方式不同 他们开始告诉我 他们的经历, 或他们妹妹的经历, 或他们朋友的经历。

sentences.en: Things are different because now I know that depression is the family secret that everyone has.
sentences.zh: 事情不同了,因为现在我知道 抑郁症是每个人的家庭秘密

sentences.en: I went a few years ago to a conference, and on Friday of the three-day conference, one of the participants took me aside, and she said, "I suffer from depression and I'm a little embarrassed about it,
sentences.zh: 几年前我去参加一个会议, 星期五的三天会议, 一位与会者把我拉到一边, 她说,“我患有抑郁症,我有点尴尬,

sentences.en: but I've been taking this medication, and I just wanted to ask you what you think?"
sentences.zh: 但我一直在吃这种药 我只想问你你怎么想?"

sentences.en: And so I did my best to give her such advice as I could.
sentences.zh: 所以我尽力给了她这样的忠告

sentences.en: And then she said, "You know, my husband would never understand this.
sentences.zh: 然后她说,"你知道, 我丈夫永远不会明白这一点。

sentences.en: He's really the kind of guy to whom this wouldn't make any sense, so, you know, it's just between us."
sentences.zh: 他真的是那种人,对这没有任何意义, 所以,你知道,这只是我们之间的事。”

sentences.en: And I said, "Yes, that's fine." On Sunday of the same conference, her husband took me aside, (Laughter) and he said, "My wife wouldn't think that I was really much of a guy if she knew this, but I've been dealing with this depression and I'm taking some medication,
sentences.zh: 我说,“是的,那很好。”在同一次会议的星期天, 她的丈夫把我拉到一边, (笑声) 他说,“我的妻子不会认为我是一个真正的男人 如果她知道这一点,

sentences.en: and I wondered what you think?" They were hiding the same medication in two different places in the same bedroom.
sentences.zh: 他们把同样的药藏在同一个卧室的两个不同的地方。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I said that I thought communication within the marriage might be triggering some of their problems.
sentences.zh: 我说我觉得婚姻内部的沟通 可能会引发他们的一些问题

sentences.en: (Laughter) But I was also struck by the burdensome nature of such mutual secrecy.
sentences.zh: 但我也为这种相互保密的烦恼感到吃惊。

sentences.en: Depression is so exhausting. It takes up so much of your time and energy, and silence about it, it really does make the depression worse.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症是如此的疲惫。它占用了这么多的时间和精力, 并且对此保持沉默,它确实使抑郁症更加恶化。

sentences.en: And then I began thinking about all the ways people make themselves better.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始思考人们如何让自己变得更好。

sentences.en: I'd started off as a medical conservative.
sentences.zh: 我一开始是个医学保守派

sentences.en: I thought there were a few kinds of therapy that worked, it was clear what they were -- there was medication, there were certain psychotherapies, there was possibly electroconvulsive treatment, and that everything else was nonsense.
sentences.zh: 我以为有几种疗法起作用了, 很明显它们是什么—— 有药物,有某些心理治疗, 可能有电休克疗法, 而其他一切都是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: But then I discovered something. If you have brain cancer, and you say that standing on your head for 20 minutes every morning makes you feel better, it may make you feel better, but you still have brain cancer, and you'll still probably die from it.
sentences.zh: 但是后来我发现了一些东西。如果你得了脑癌, 你说每天早上站在你的头上20分钟 让你感觉好些, 可能会让你感觉好些, 但你还是得了脑癌, 你可能还是会死于脑癌。

sentences.en: But if you say that you have depression, and standing on your head for 20 minutes every day makes you feel better, then it's worked, because depression is an illness of how you feel, and if you feel better, then you are effectively not depressed anymore.
sentences.zh: 但如果你说你患有抑郁症, 并且每天站在你的头上20分钟 让你感觉好一点, 那么它就起作用了, 因为抑郁症是一种疾病 你的感觉,如果你感觉好一点, 那么实际上你不再沮丧了。

sentences.en: So I became much more tolerant of the vast world of alternative treatments.
sentences.zh: 所以,我变得更宽容 广阔的世界 替代治疗。

sentences.en: And I get letters, I get hundreds of letters from people writing to tell me about what's worked for them.
sentences.zh: 我收到信,我收到数百封信 来告诉我什么是他们的工作。

sentences.en: Someone was asking me backstage today about meditation.
sentences.zh: 今天有人在后台问我冥想的事

sentences.en: My favorite of the letters that I got was the one that came from a woman who wrote and said that she had tried therapy, medication, she had tried pretty much everything, and she had found a solution and hoped I would tell the world,
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的信 是来自一个女人的 写下来说她尝试了治疗和药物, 她几乎尝试了一切, 她已经找到了一个解决方案, 希望我会告诉全世界,

sentences.en: and that was making little things from yarn.
sentences.zh: 这是小小东西 从缝线。

sentences.en: (Laughter) She sent me some of them. (Laughter) And I'm not wearing them right now.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 她给我寄了一些。 (笑) 而且我没有穿他们现在。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I suggested to her that she also should look up obsessive compulsive disorder in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 我建议她也去DSM检查 强迫性失调症

sentences.en: And yet, when I went to look at alternative treatments, I also gained perspective on other treatments.
sentences.zh: 然而,当我去研究替代治疗方法时,我对其他治疗方法也有了认识。

sentences.en: I went through a tribal exorcism in Senegal that involved a great deal of ram's blood and that I'm not going to detail right now, but a few years afterwards I was in Rwanda, working on a different project, and I happened to describe my experience to someone,
sentences.zh: 我在塞内加尔经历了一场部落驱魔, 涉及到大量的公羊的血液, 我现在不打算细说, 但几年后我在卢旺达, 在一个不同的项目, 我碰巧描述了我的经验给某人,

sentences.en: and he said, "Well, that's West Africa, and we're in East Africa, and our rituals are in some ways very different, but we do have some rituals that have something in common with what you're describing."
sentences.zh: 他说:“嗯,这是西非, 我们在东非, 我们的仪式在某些方面非常不同, 但是我们有一些仪式, 与你所描述的东西有共同之处。”

sentences.en: And he said, "But we've had a lot of trouble with Western mental health workers, especially the ones who came right after the genocide."
sentences.zh: 他说,“但是我们和西方精神卫生工作者 有过很多麻烦, 特别是那些在种族灭绝之后刚来的人。”

sentences.en: I said, "What kind of trouble did you have?"
sentences.zh: 我说,"你有什么麻烦?"

sentences.en: And he said, "Well, they would do this bizarre thing.
sentences.zh: 他说,"嗯,他们会做这个奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: They didn't take people out in the sunshine where you begin to feel better.
sentences.zh: 他们没有在阳光下带人出去 在那里你开始感觉更好。

sentences.en: They didn't include drumming or music to get people's blood going.
sentences.zh: 他们没有包括鼓声或音乐 让人们的血流成河

sentences.en: They didn't involve the whole community.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把整个社区都扯进来

sentences.en: They didn't externalize the depression as an invasive spirit.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把抑郁症 外部化为一种侵入精神。

sentences.en: Instead what they did was they took people one at a time into dingy little rooms and had them talk for an hour about bad things that had happened to them."
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的是,他们把人们一个一个一个 关进一个破房间 让他们谈了一个小时的坏事 发生在他们身上。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) He said, "We had to ask them to leave the country."
sentences.zh: 他说,“我们必须要求他们离开这个国家。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now at the other end of alternative treatments, let me tell you about Frank Russakoff.
sentences.zh: （笑声）现在，在替代疗法的另一端，让我告诉你关于弗兰克·鲁萨科夫（Frank Russakoff）的事。

sentences.en: Frank Russakoff had the worst depression perhaps that I've ever seen in a man.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·鲁萨科夫（Frank Russakoff）的抑郁症可能是我见过的最严重的男人。

sentences.en: He was constantly depressed. He was, when I met him, at a point at which every month, he would have electroshock treatment.
sentences.zh: 他一直郁郁寡欢。当我遇见他时，他每个月都会接受电击治疗。

sentences.en: Then he would feel sort of disoriented for a week.
sentences.zh: 然后他会在一周内感到某种迷失方向。

sentences.en: Then he would feel okay for a week. Then he would have a week of going downhill.
sentences.zh: 然后他会感觉好一个星期。然后他将有一周的时间走下坡路。

sentences.en: And then he would have another electroshock treatment.
sentences.zh: 然后他将接受另一次电击治疗。

sentences.en: And he said to me when I met him, "It's unbearable to go through my weeks this way.
sentences.zh: 当我见到他时，他对我说：“以这种方式度过我的几周真是难以忍受。

sentences.en: I can't go on this way, and I've figured out how I'm going to end it if I don't get better."
sentences.zh: 我不能再这样下去了，我已经想好了如果我没有好转的话我该如何结束它。”

sentences.en: "But," he said to me, "I heard about a protocol at Mass General for a procedure called a cingulotomy, which is a brain surgery, and I think I'm going to give that a try."
sentences.zh: “但是，”他对我说，“我听说麻省总医院有一项名为扣带回切开术的手术方案，这是一种脑部手术，我想我会尝试一下。”

sentences.en: And I remember being amazed at that point to think that someone who clearly had so many bad experiences with so many different treatments still had buried in him, somewhere, enough optimism to reach out for one more.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我很惊讶地想到，一个显然经历了如此多糟糕经历和如此多不同治疗方法的人仍然在他内心的某个地方埋藏着足够的乐观情绪，以寻求再一次的治疗。

sentences.en: And he had the cingulotomy, and it was incredibly successful.
sentences.zh: 他做了扣带回切开术，非常成功。

sentences.en: He's now a friend of mine. He has a lovely wife and two beautiful children.
sentences.zh: 他现在是我的朋友了。他有一个可爱的妻子和两个漂亮的孩子。

sentences.en: He wrote me a letter the Christmas after the surgery, and he said, "My father sent me two presents this year, First, a motorized CD rack from The Sharper Image that I didn't really need, but I knew he was giving it to me to celebrate
sentences.zh: 手术后的圣诞节，他给我写了一封信，他说：“我父亲今年给我送了两件礼物，第一是 The Sharper Image 的电动 CD 架，我并不真正需要，但我知道他送给我是为了庆祝

sentences.en: the fact that I'm living on my own and have a job I seem to love.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我独自生活并且有一份我似乎喜欢的工作。

sentences.en: And the other present was a photo of my grandmother, who committed suicide.
sentences.zh: 另一件礼物是我祖母的照片，她自杀了。

sentences.en: As I unwrapped it, I began to cry, and my mother came over and said, 'Are you crying because of the relatives you never knew?'
sentences.zh: 当我拆开它的时候，我开始哭了，我妈妈走过来说：“你是因为那些素不相识的亲戚而哭吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, 'She had the same disease I have.'
sentences.zh: 我说：“她和我有同样的病。”

sentences.en: I'm crying now as I write to you. It's not that I'm so sad, but I get overwhelmed, I think, because I could have killed myself, but my parents kept me going, and so did the doctors, and I had the surgery.
sentences.zh: 当我给你写信时，我现在哭了。我并不是那么悲伤，而是我感到不知所措，因为我本可以自杀，但我的父母让我坚持下去，医生也是如此，我接受了手术。

sentences.en: I'm alive and grateful. We live in the right time, even if it doesn't always feel like it."
sentences.zh: 我还活着并且心存感激。我们生活在正确的时代，尽管感觉并不总是如此。”

sentences.en: I was struck by the fact that depression is broadly perceived to be a modern, Western, middle-class thing, and I went to look at how it operated in a variety of other contexts, and one of the things I was most interested in
sentences.zh: 令我震惊的是，抑郁症被广泛认为是一种现代的、西方的、中产阶级的事物，我去研究它在各种其他情况下是如何运作的，这是我最感兴趣的事情之一

sentences.en: was depression among the indigent. And so I went out to try to look at what was being done for poor people with depression.
sentences.zh: 是穷人中的抑郁症。所以我出去尝试看看正在为患有抑郁症的穷人做些什么。

sentences.en: And what I discovered is that poor people are mostly not being treated for depression.
sentences.zh: 我发现穷人大多没有接受抑郁症治疗。

sentences.en: Depression is the result of a genetic vulnerability, which is presumably evenly distributed in the population, and triggering circumstances, which are likely to be more severe for people who are impoverished.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症是遗传脆弱性的结果，这种脆弱性大概在人群中均匀分布，并且引发环境，对于贫困人口来说可能更为严重。

sentences.en: And yet it turns out that if you have a really lovely life but feel miserable all the time, you think, "Why do I feel like this?
sentences.zh: 然而事实证明，如果你的生活非常美好，但却总是感到痛苦，你会想：“为什么我会有这样的感觉？

sentences.en: I must have depression." And you set out to find treatment for it.
sentences.zh: 我一定是得了抑郁症。”你开始寻找治疗方法。

sentences.en: But if you have a perfectly awful life, and you feel miserable all the time, the way you feel is commensurate with your life, and it doesn't occur to you to think, "Maybe this is treatable."
sentences.zh: 但如果你的生活非常糟糕, 并且你总是感到痛苦, 你的感觉与你的生活是相称的, 你并没有想到, “也许这是可以治疗的。”

sentences.en: And so we have an epidemic in this country of depression among impoverished people that's not being picked up and that's not being treated and that's not being addressed, and it's a tragedy of a grand order.
sentences.zh: 因此,我们有一个流行病 在这个国家的萧条 穷人没有被拾起, 没有得到治疗, 没有得到解决, 这是一个悲剧 一个大秩序。

sentences.en: And so I found an academic who was doing a research project in slums outside of D.C., where she picked up women who had come in for other health problems and diagnosed them with depression, and then provided six months of the experimental protocol.
sentences.zh: 于是我发现一个学者 正在华盛顿特区以外的贫民窟里做一个研究项目, 她在那里接了那些 来找其他健康问题的妇女, 诊断她们患有抑郁症, 然后提供了六个月的实验协议。

sentences.en: One of them, Lolly, came in, and this is what she said the day she came in.
sentences.zh: 其中一个叫Lolly 进来了 她进来那天就是这么说的

sentences.en: She said, and she was a woman, by the way, who had seven children.
sentences.zh: 她说,她是一个女人,顺便说一句, 她有七个孩子。

sentences.en: She said, "I used to have a job but I had to give it up because I couldn't go out of the house.
sentences.zh: 她说,"我曾经有一份工作,但我不得不放弃它 因为我不能走出家门。

sentences.en: I have nothing to say to my children. In the morning, I can't wait for them to leave, and then I climb in bed and pull the covers over my head, and three o'clock when they come home, it just comes so fast."
sentences.zh: 我没有话要对我的孩子说。早上,我等不及要他们离开, 然后我爬到床上,把盖子拉到我头上, 当他们回家的时候,三点钟,它就来得太快了。”

sentences.en: She said, "I've been taking a lot of Tylenol, anything I can take so that I can sleep more.
sentences.zh: 她说,"我吃了很多泰伦诺, 任何我可以吃的东西,这样我就可以睡得更久。

sentences.en: My husband has been telling me I'm stupid, I'm ugly.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫一直告诉我我很蠢,我很丑

sentences.en: I wish I could stop the pain." Well, she was brought into this experimental protocol, and when I interviewed her six months later, she had taken a job working in childcare
sentences.zh: 我希望我能止痛" 她被引入了这个实验协议 我六个月后采访她时 她就找了份育儿工作

sentences.en: for the U.S. Navy, she had left the abusive husband, and she said to me, "My kids are so much happier now."
sentences.zh: 对于美国海军来说, 她离开了那个虐待丈夫, 她对我说, “我的孩子现在更加幸福了。”

sentences.en: She said, "There's one room in my new place for the boys and one room for the girls, but at night, they're just all up on my bed, and we're doing homework all together and everything.
sentences.zh: 她说,“我的新地方有一个房间给男孩们, 一个房间给女孩们, 但是在晚上,他们都在我的床上, 我们一起做功课。

sentences.en: One of them wants to be a preacher, one of them wants to be a firefighter, and one of the girls says she's going to be a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 其中一个想当传教士 其中一个想当消防员 有个女孩说她要当律师

sentences.en: They don't cry like they used to, and they don't fight like they did.
sentences.zh: 他们不像以前那样哭 也不像以前那样打架

sentences.en: That's all I need now, is my kids. Things keep on changing, the way I dress, the way I feel, the way I act.
sentences.zh: 我现在需要的就是我的孩子 不断的改变,我穿衣的方式,我的感觉,我的行为方式

sentences.en: I can go outside not being afraid anymore, and I don't think those bad feelings are coming back, and if it weren't for Dr. Miranda and that, I would still be at home with the covers pulled over my head,
sentences.zh: 我可以出去 不再害怕了, 而且我不认为 那些不好的感觉 回来了, 如果不是米兰达博士,

sentences.en: if I were still alive at all. I asked the Lord to send me an angel, and He heard my prayers."
sentences.zh: 如果我还活著,我求主派一个天神来给我,他听见我的祈祷了。

sentences.en: I was really moved by these experiences, and I decided that I wanted to write about them not only in a book I was working on, but also in an article, and I got a commission from The New York Times Magazine to write about depression among the indigent.
sentences.zh: 我为这些经历感到很感动, 我决定不仅要在一本书里写下这些经历, 还要在一篇文章里写下, 我从《纽约时报》得到一个委托, 来写关于穷人的抑郁症。

sentences.en: And I turned in my story, and my editor called me and said, "We really can't publish this."
sentences.zh: 我翻阅了我的故事, 我的编辑打电话给我说, "我们真的不能出版这个。"

sentences.en: And I said, "Why not?" And she said, "It just is too far-fetched.
sentences.zh: 我说,“为什么不呢?”她说,“这太牵强了。

sentences.en: These people who are sort of at the very bottom rung of society and then they get a few months of treatment and they're virtually ready to run Morgan Stanley?
sentences.zh: 这些人在社会最底层 得到几个月的治疗 他们几乎准备好管理摩根斯坦利了?

sentences.en: It's just too implausible." She said, "I've never even heard of anything like it."
sentences.zh: 太难以置信了 她说 "我从没听过这样的事"

sentences.en: And I said, "The fact that you've never heard of it is an indication that it is news."
sentences.zh: 我说,“你从未听说过的事实 表明这是新闻。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) "And you are a news magazine."
sentences.zh: (笑) (掌声) "你是一个新闻杂志。"

sentences.en: So after a certain amount of negotiation, they agreed to it.
sentences.zh: 所以经过一定的谈判 他们同意了

sentences.en: But I think a lot of what they said was connected in some strange way to this distaste that people still have for the idea of treatment, the notion that somehow if we went out and treated a lot of people in indigent communities,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们所说的很多内容都以某种奇怪的方式与人们仍然对治疗理念的厌恶联系在一起，即如果我们出去治疗贫困社区的很多人，

sentences.en: that would be exploitative, because we would be changing them.
sentences.zh: 这将是一种剥削，因为我们会改变它们。

sentences.en: There is this false moral imperative that seems to be all around us, that treatment of depression, the medications and so on, are an artifice, and that it's not natural.
sentences.zh: 我们周围似乎存在着这种错误的道德要求，即抑郁症的治疗、药物等都是一种技巧，而且是不自然的。

sentences.en: And I think that's very misguided. It would be natural for people's teeth to fall out, but there is nobody militating against toothpaste, at least not in my circles.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是非常误导的。人们的牙齿脱落是很自然的事，但没有人反对使用牙膏，至少在我的圈子里没有。

sentences.en: People then say, "But isn't depression part of what people are supposed to experience?
sentences.zh: 人们然后会说：“但是抑郁症不是人们应该经历的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Didn't we evolve to have depression? Isn't it part of your personality?"
sentences.zh: 难道我们进化而来就没有抑郁症吗？这难道不是你性格的一部分吗？”

sentences.en: To which I would say, mood is adaptive. Being able to have sadness and fear and joy and pleasure and all of the other moods that we have, that's incredibly valuable.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，情绪是适应性的。能够拥有悲伤、恐惧、喜悦和愉悦以及我们拥有的所有其他情绪，这是非常有价值的。

sentences.en: And major depression is something that happens when that system gets broken.
sentences.zh: 当该系统被破坏时，就会发生严重抑郁症。

sentences.en: It's maladaptive. People will come to me and say, "I think, though, if I just stick it out for another year, I think I can just get through this."
sentences.zh: 这是适应不良。人们会来找我说：“不过，我想，如果我再坚持一年，我想我就能渡过难关。”

sentences.en: And I always say to them, "You may get through it, but you'll never be 37 again.
sentences.zh: 我总是对他们说：“你可能会挺过去，但你再也不会回到 37 岁了。

sentences.en: Life is short, and that's a whole year you're talking about giving up.
sentences.zh: 人生苦短，这一整年你都在谈论放弃。

sentences.en: Think it through." It's a strange poverty of the English language, and indeed of many other languages, that we use this same word, depression, to describe how a kid feels when it rains on his birthday,
sentences.zh: 想清楚了。”这是英语的一种奇怪的贫乏，实际上也是许多其他语言的一种奇怪的贫乏，我们用同一个词“抑郁”来描述一个孩子在生日那天下雨时的感受，

sentences.en: and to describe how somebody feels the minute before they commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 并描述某人自杀前一刻的感受。

sentences.en: People say to me, "Well, is it continuous with normal sadness?"
sentences.zh: 人们对我说：“嗯，这是持续的正常悲伤吗？”

sentences.en: And I say, in a way it's continuous with normal sadness.
sentences.zh: 我说，在某种程度上，它与正常的悲伤是连续的。

sentences.en: There is a certain amount of continuity, but it's the same way there's continuity between having an iron fence outside your house that gets a little rust spot that you have to sand off and do a little repainting, and what happens if you leave the house for 100 years
sentences.zh: 存在一定程度的连续性，但就像你房子外面有铁栅栏，上面有一点锈迹，你必须用砂纸磨掉并重新粉刷一下，以及如果你离开房子 100 年会发生什么之间存在连续性一样。

sentences.en: and it rusts through until it's only a pile of orange dust.
sentences.zh: 它会生锈，直到变成一堆橙色的灰尘。

sentences.en: And it's that orange dust spot, that orange dust problem, that's the one we're setting out to address.
sentences.zh: 这就是橙色尘点，橙色尘埃问题，这就是我们要解决的问题。

sentences.en: So now people say, "You take these happy pills, and do you feel happy?"
sentences.zh: 所以现在人们说，“你吃了这些快乐药丸，你感到快乐吗？”

sentences.en: And I don't. But I don't feel sad about having to eat lunch, and I don't feel sad about my answering machine, and I don't feel sad about taking a shower.
sentences.zh: 但我不这么认为。但我不会因为要吃午饭而感到难过，不会因为电话答录机而感到难过，也不会因为洗澡而感到难过。

sentences.en: I feel more, in fact, I think, because I can feel sadness without nullity.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想，我的感受更多，因为我可以感受到悲伤而不是空虚。

sentences.en: I feel sad about professional disappointments, about damaged relationships, about global warming.
sentences.zh: 我对职业上的失望、人际关系的破坏和全球变暖感到悲伤。

sentences.en: Those are the things that I feel sad about now.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我现在感到难过的事情。

sentences.en: And I said to myself, well, what is the conclusion?
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，好吧，结论是什么？

sentences.en: How did those people who have better lives even with bigger depression manage to get through?
sentences.zh: 那些抑郁症严重但生活却更好的人是如何度过的？

sentences.en: What is the mechanism of resilience? And what I came up with over time was that the people who deny their experience, and say, "I was depressed a long time ago, I never want to think about it again, I'm not going to look at it
sentences.zh: 恢复力机制是什么? 随着时间的推移,我想到的是那些否认自己经验的人, 并且说,“我很久前就沮丧了, 我再也不想再想了, 我不想再去想它了。

sentences.en: and I'm just going to get on with my life," ironically, those are the people who are most enslaved by what they have.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是, 这些人被他们拥有的东西奴役得最多。

sentences.en: Shutting out the depression strengthens it.
sentences.zh: 消除忧郁会加强它。

sentences.en: While you hide from it, it grows. And the people who do better are the ones who are able to tolerate the fact that they have this condition.
sentences.zh: 当你躲开它的时候,它却在增长。那些做得更好的人,是那些能够忍受自己有这种病的人。

sentences.en: Those who can tolerate their depression are the ones who achieve resilience.
sentences.zh: 那些能够忍受抑郁症的人就是那些能够实现复原力的人。

sentences.en: So Frank Russakoff said to me, "If I had a do-over, I suppose I wouldn't do it this way, but in a strange way, I'm grateful for what I've experienced.
sentences.zh: Frank Russakoff对我说,“如果我做了一次, 我想我不会这样做, 但奇怪的是,我很感激我所经历的。

sentences.en: I'm glad to have been in the hospital 40 times.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴在医院呆了40次

sentences.en: It taught me so much about love, and my relationship with my parents and my doctors has been so precious to me, and will be always."
sentences.zh: 它教会了我很多关于爱的事情, 我与我的父母和医生的关系 对我来说是如此珍贵, 并且将永远如此。”

sentences.en: And Maggie Robbins said, "I used to volunteer in an AIDS clinic, and I would just talk and talk and talk, and the people I was dealing with weren't very responsive, and I thought, 'That's not very friendly or helpful of them.'"
sentences.zh: Maggie Robbins说,“我过去在艾滋病诊所当志愿者, 我会说话,说话,说话, 和我打交道的人反应不灵敏, 我想,“那对他们不怎么友好,也没有帮助。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "And then I realized, I realized that they weren't going to do more than make those first few minutes of small talk.
sentences.zh: "然后我意识到,我意识到, 他们不会做的更多 仅仅做那些头几分钟的小谈话。

sentences.en: It was simply going to be an occasion where I didn't have AIDS and I wasn't dying, but could tolerate the fact that they did and they were.
sentences.zh: 它只是会是一个场合 我没有艾滋病,我没有死, 但能够容忍的事实, 他们做到了,他们是。

sentences.en: Our needs are our greatest assets. It turns out I've learned to give all the things I need."
sentences.zh: 我们的需要是我们最大的财富, 结果我学会了给予我所需要的一切。”

sentences.en: Valuing one's depression does not prevent a relapse, but it may make the prospect of relapse and even relapse itself easier to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 重视抑郁症并不能防止复发,但可能导致复发,甚至复发本身更容易被容忍。

sentences.en: The question is not so much of finding great meaning and deciding your depression has been very meaningful.
sentences.zh: 问题并不在于 找到伟大的意义 并且决定你的抑郁症 是非常有意义的。

sentences.en: It's of seeking that meaning and thinking, when it comes again, "This will be hellish, but I will learn something from it."
sentences.zh: 这是寻求这个意义 和思考, 当它再次出现, "这将是地狱般的, 但我会从它学到一些东西。"

sentences.en: I have learned in my own depression how big an emotion can be, how it can be more real than facts, and I have found that experience has allowed me to experience positive emotion
sentences.zh: 我从自己的忧郁中了解到 情绪能有多大 如何比事实更真实 并且我发现 经验使我得以体验到积极的情感

sentences.en: in a more intense and more focused way. The opposite of depression is not happiness, but vitality, and these days, my life is vital, even on the days when I'm sad.
sentences.zh: 更强烈,更集中。 抑郁的反面不是幸福,而是活力,这些日子,我的人生至关重要,即使在我悲伤的日子。

sentences.en: I felt that funeral in my brain, and I sat next to the colossus at the edge of the world, and I have discovered something inside of myself that I would have to call a soul
sentences.zh: 我在我的大脑里感觉到葬礼, 我坐在世界边缘的巨人旁边, 我发现了自己内心的一些东西, 我不得不叫一个人的灵魂

sentences.en: that I had never formulated until that day 20 years ago when hell came to pay me a surprise visit.
sentences.zh: 直到20年前的那天 地狱突然来拜访我

sentences.en: I think that while I hated being depressed and would hate to be depressed again, I've found a way to love my depression.
sentences.zh: 我觉得,虽然我讨厌 沮丧和讨厌再次沮丧, 我已经找到了一个方法 爱我的抑郁。

sentences.en: I love it because it has forced me to find and cling to joy.
sentences.zh: 我爱它,因为它迫使我 找到并坚持喜悦。

sentences.en: I love it because each day I decide, sometimes gamely, and sometimes against the moment's reason, to cleave to the reasons for living.
sentences.zh: 我爱它,因为每天我决定, 有时是游戏性的, 有时是违背当时的理由, 屈从于生活的理由。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is a highly privileged rapture.
sentences.zh: 我认为,这是一个非常优雅的喜悦。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause) Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: (掌声) 谢谢。 (掌声)
